text:
Morgan - People Ops: quick q — Jamal asked to make an out-of-cycle comp increase + title change effective 3/1 for an EMEA IC who started 3/10. Manager wants retro to start of month so payroll line-up is simpler. Is that allowed and what paperwork do we need? cc @Jamal :thinking:

Jamal - Eng Manager: yep — they started 3/10 but the ask is to make the comp increase effective 3/1. candidate accepted w/ verbal earlier. trying to avoid backpay calc headaches for finance.

Elena - Comp Analyst: short answer: we can set an effective date earlier than start in most locations, but two things to check: tax/reg local regs (some countries treat pay for days before actual start differently) and equity/grant docs — the grant effective date must match eligibility.

Priya - Payroll: procedural: if effective < start_date we need a manager justification + signed offer amendment. payroll will process retro pay only after docs clear and within payroll cutoff. For example, our payroll command for manual adjustment is:

```
run_payroll_adjust --employee 98765 --period 2026-03 --retro-start 2026-03-01 --reason "comp change effective date" --amount <calculated-backpay>
```

But do NOT run until People Ops confirms docs + tax signoff. Cutoff for March run is 2026-03-25 PST.

Alex - HRBP: tagging legal for cross-border: some jurisdictions require the employee to have been on payroll to receive pay that predates start. If the hire date is after the effective date, we need Legal ok or use a separate one-time sign-on adjustment that references hire date.

Morgan - People Ops: action checklist I'm proposing: 1) Manager attaches signed offer amendment (dates + reason). 2) Comp to confirm net backpay calc and equity effective date sync. 3) Payroll to confirm cutoffs and run window. 4) Legal check for country-specific rule. 5) People Ops files docs. Anyone object?

Jamal - Eng Manager: fine. I can get the signed amendment today. Quick Q on backpay calc: do you pro-rate by days or calendar month?

Elena - Comp Analyst: we always pro-rate by actual days worked in the period unless comp policy says full-month on effective date. Formula we use:

```
backpay = (new_annual / 12 / days_in_month) * days_eligible - (old_annual / 12 / days_in_month) * days_eligible
```

where days_eligible = days between effective_date and hire_or_period_end inclusive. Example: effective 3/1, hire 3/10 -> days_eligible = 9 (3/1-3/9) for retro pay.

Priya - Payroll: note — for EMEA we also withhold differently; payroll will produce a tax memo for the comp team. If the amount is > threshold, we need manager approval for the one-time adj in the payroll UI.

Morgan - People Ops: flags: 1) Equity grants: if grant date < hire date, comp needs to confirm grant approach (we usually set grant effective to actual start or to grant approval date to avoid compliance issues). 2) Benefits enrollment: benefits eligibility typically starts on hire date; we cannot enroll someone for coverage prior to their first day. So benefits cannot be retro-applied. Make sure manager knows.

Jamal - Eng Manager: ok noted — benefits can't be predated. For equity, they'd prefer grant effective 3/1 to match comp. Is that a showstopper?

Alex - HRBP: often easier to have grant effective = hire_date and add a note that comp was set effective earlier for salary only. Legal/Comp should confirm. If the grant affects vesting schedules, don't backdate.

people-bot: Reminder: payroll cutoff in 4 days (2026-03-25 23:59 PST) :bell:

Morgan - People Ops: next steps: Jamal to upload signed amendment to the HR folder + ping here when done. Elena will run a draft backpay calc and equity note. Priya will confirm payroll window and the run command. Alex to route to Legal if EMEA country flagged. I'll close the thread when docs are in folder. Thanks! :white_check_mark:
